own_solution.law: Thin-rod longitudinal wave speed c = sqrt(E/rho); free-free fundamental with central clamp: lambda_rod = 2L, f = c/(2L); air standing wave node spacing = lambda_air/2 = v_air/(2f) = v_air*L/c
assumptions: light disc does not load the rod
air column resonant at rod frequency

notes: c = sqrt(7e10/2700) = 5091.75 m/s; f = 5091.75/2.4 = 2121.6 Hz; spacing = 343/(2*2121.6) = 0.080837 m (8.08 cm). With L = 1.52 m (clamp fitted at the middle of the extended rod): 343*1.52/5091.75 = 0.10239 m. Cross-section/diameter appear in mass and stiffness and cancel from c = sqrt(E/rho) (C, valid while the rod stays thin compared with the wavelength: 8 mm vs 2.4 m). Railing and 'earlier run only' sentences are D. Note: a diameter of 8.21 mm gives 0.529 cm^2, not 1.6 cm^2, but these are separate sentences each added alone, so no within-item contradiction. Variant pairs T94AF/T9574 (8.21 mm) and T641F/T1BAE (1.6 cm^2) state the same values. TFBD6 and TFE55 carry no number ('small amount', 'a few centimetres').
